stem: Let $n_1(x)=\frac{x^2(x+{=q})}{x^2(x-{=p})(x+{=q})}$ and $n_2(x)=\frac{x^3+{=p}x^2+{=c2}x}{x^4-{=c3}x}$, where $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Both fractions have the same simplest form, but $n_1\neq n_2$. Find the sum of the real values of $x$ that are excluded from the common domain of $n_1$ and $n_2$.
solution: Simplify $n_1$: cancelling $x^2(x+{=q})$ gives $n_1(x)=\frac{1}{x-{=p}}$. Its domain is $\mathbb{R}-\{0, {=p}, -{=q}\}$.
So $n_2(x)=\frac{1}{x-{=p}}$. The factor $x^2+{=p}x+{=c2}$ is never zero for real $x$, so the domain of $n_2$ is $\mathbb{R}-\{0, {=p}\}$.
The domains differ, so $n_1\neq n_2$. The common domain is $\mathbb{R}-\{0, {=p}, -{=q}\}$.
The excluded values are $0$, ${=p}$ and $-{=q}$; their sum is ${=p-q}$.
notes: x^2+px+p^2 has negative discriminant (-3p^2) so no real roots. p!=q gives nonzero sum; sum may be negative.
